doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Do today's players equal the old ones? Chords and substitutions
summary: Budd explains chord construction and how modern players substitute chords by ear.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Oh my. How has the music — the music we’re hearing today at festivals like this, do you think it’s stood the test of time? Do you think that the players of today are of the same caliber?
In what way? Quality or character or inspiration?
Actually, just in their musicianship I think.

I don’t think so. But maybe they know more than I do. They can take chords and it seems to me, if you understand a chord, you take the first, the third and the fifth and the seventh. C is the first, C, D, E is the second, F, G is the third, and B is the fourth and you flat the B it becomes a seventh chord. And above the B flat the next is D is the ninth and F is the eleventh, and A is the thirteenth, and back to C is the fifteenth. And I think some of these guys, they substitute chords. They play a chord in C but instead of playing the basic C they play the fourth, the sixth and the eleventh, and say what’s that. And they have such ear. I don’t know what they’re doing but that’s how they explain it.
